title: Art Style Consistency & Volume
author: jjmwisco2016
selftext:
I am trying to create consistent-styled card art for my CCG, and after spending money on not a great outcome I am curious if anything is working well for ppl right now.

I tried using Scenario AI with their model training option, but after a ton of credit usage and attempts the model either didn’t capture the style fully, or it produced overfitted results and didn’t respond well to new prompts. 

Midjourney looks like a potential option for style consistency but I don’t like how you have to pay $60 a month for “stealth mode” generation so your art isn’t publicly listed on their explore page. There’s also no free trial rn and don’t want to pay if it doesn’t work. 

My only other idea is to create an AI agent flow that can generate the art, use a style guide Skill or something, and build an ad hoc solution. 

Anyone have advice for tools/sites I should check out? Or is the answer “the current options aren’t good right now, check back in 6 months once models improve”?

comments.author: angelarose210
comments.body:
Comfyui using qwen image edit 2511 with style transfer. Look on r/StableDiffusion or r/comfyui
I use comfyui via api for production workflows and generate hundreds of images a day. It's very consistent once you get your prompt engineering down.

replies.author: jjmwisco2016
replies.body: Ooo just started browsing them and this looks like a good direction to go in, thanks!

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
This probably won’t be too helpful but here is how I am doing it with my game and with great results.

I’m doing pixel art with minimal shading, 2-d sidescroller perspective with just 32 colors. 

My extreme limitations has brought cohesion to my art style. It’s so simple that it’s almost hard for things to look out of place. Been doing a good amount of editing though.

I’ve found that it’s pretty tricky to get generations to fit the art style I want so my solution was to make the art style so simple that all it takes is a little manual editing if something doesn’t look like it fits my game.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for assets such as spritesheets, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio (https://gamelabstudio.co). It’s designed for game assets and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything.

Gamelabs Studio MCP plugs right into your agent like Cursor, to enable rapid iteration right in your code editor

https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

replies.author: Early_Situation_6552
replies.body:
>because AI models cant output transparency

this is 100% false. they definitely can and are much more likely to if you request it

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Try it. Ask nano banana for a picture of a banana on a transparent background. It’s just a fully opaque checkerboard that isn’t transparent

https://preview.redd.it/jux48w085fvg1.jpeg?width=1179&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=e91d1e5422d6f74b88d917e109c527d7b16a18ec

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body: Yes! While ChatGPT sometimes outputs an image that has a transparent background when requested, what’s it’s actually doing is generating an image, and then using python to cut out the background. You can tell because inside text chars like “a” and “o” for instance it’s still got the white background inside them

replies.author: Early_Situation_6552
replies.body: nah the person you're replying to doesn't know what they're talking about. ChatGPT can definitely output alpha (transparency) channels without using a python script

replies.author: angelarose210
replies.body: In comfyui you simply need to add a rmbg node to remove the background and give you transparency.  I have a nano banana workflow that does this.

replies.author: Early_Situation_6552
replies.body:
i don't know why you're showing me your failed attempt on one model as support for the claim "AI models cant output transparency". i also don't know why you're trying to educate others on this when you clearly don't understand it

they can definitely do alpha channels, and no, it's not just a python background removal script. here you go

https://preview.redd.it/gpwxitlv5hvg1.png?width=1536&format=png&auto=webp&s=c53e0e974376eec7c82fb060127b38d5aefb6f3f

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body: You’re not wrong. There are definitely ai models capable of outputting alpha channels like RMBG for instance, which takes in an input image and segments it to remove the background.

comments.author: FFKUSES
comments.body: style consistency at volume is the hard part with card games. comfyui with a finetuned SDXL model gives you the most control but the setup time is real. for something faster, Mage Space (mage.space) handles batch generation well under a flat membership so you're not burning credits per card.
